lessons.title: The same four lines, with a clock
lessons.gloss: the same four lines with a clock running, against the published DELE A1 writing timing and criteria

notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your hands, so it is not a driving lesson. You can listen to all of it now and come back to the parts that need looking at once you have stopped.

segments.text: You wrote four lines about yourself with as long as you liked.
A task you can only do untimed is not yet a task you can do. Here are the exam's own conditions.

What the exam publishes. The DELE A1 writing paper runs 25 minutes and holds two tasks. The first is a personal-information form asking for 15 to 25 words. No dictionary. No phone. You write in the booklet you are given.
That is one task out of two, so give it its share and no more: three minutes, starting now.
Write the four lines about yourself, then close with the courtesy word.
When the three minutes are up, stop writing even if a line is unfinished. An unfinished paper is information; an untimed one is not.
Now mark your own. The published criteria for this task are two, and they are worth knowing in this order:
Did you do what was asked? Four facts and a close, nothing else.
Can it be read? Language a stranger at a desk would understand. Not elegant language — understandable language.
Count your words. Under fifteen and the task is half done; well past twenty-five and you spent time you did not have. Both are worth knowing before an examiner tells you.

segments.instruction: your four lines aloud, at the pace you wrote them
segments.source: [YOU SAY: your four lines aloud, at the pace you wrote them]

segments.prompt: How long does the DELE A1 writing paper run, and how many tasks does it hold?

feedback.correct: Two tasks in twenty-five minutes, which is why one gets a share of it.

segments.prompt: The personal-information task asks for how many words?

feedback.correct: Short, and a stated range rather than a suggestion.

segments.prompt: Under the clock, write the four lines and the close.
acceptedResponses: me llamo ___. tengo ___ años. soy de ___. vivo en ___. gracias
me llamo, tengo anos, soy de, vivo en, gracias
me llamo ___. tengo ___ anos. soy de ___. vivo en ___. gracias.

feedback.correct: Four facts, a close, and inside the time.
feedback.incorrect: Me llamo, tengo ___ anos, soy de, vivo en, then gracias.

segments.text: Which of the two published criteria comes first — doing what was asked, or writing beautifully? (Doing what was asked.)
You have now written to a clock, to a word count, and to a stated standard, with no Spanish you did not already own.
